newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian Kras says 1996 results above plans.
newsitem.headline: Croatian Kras says 1996 results above plans.

text.p: Croatian chocolate maker Kras said on Monday its last year's results had overshot plans and were considerably better than those posted in 1995.
"All the figures, particularly profit, are way above our planned targets," finance director Tomislav Jovic told Reuters, adding:
"I believe shareholders will have reason to be pleased."
Jovic declined to reveal details of Kras' 1996 performance until its supervisory board approves last year's accounts, which have been audited by Price Waterhouse.
They will be ready for release in about 10 days, he said.
Kras posted a consolidated net profit of 14.8 million kuna in 1995 on total sales of 654 million kuna. The company exports some 25 percent of the total, nearly $20 million a year.

First half preliminary figures for 1996 had shown all the figures rising, while Kras managed to cut down costs. Its market position was said to have strengthened to 41 percent to August last year from 38.6 percent at the end of 1995.
Kras had also planned to invest heavily in modernisation last year so as to expand production and boost sales further.
Its stock, traded on a parallel segment of Zagreb's bourse, closed last Friday at 415 kuna -- 45 down from a week earlier. -- Kolumbina Bencevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
